description: Looking for passionate and motivated teammates for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026! We need individuals with good development skills, AI/ML knowledge, an interest in Earth Science, or a passion for exploring our planet and space. Frontend and full-stack developers, researchers, data enthusiasts, and creative problem-solvers are also welcome. Beginners and experienced participants are equally encouraged. Let's collaborate, share ideas, and build something innovative together!
summary:
AgriSmart is a NASA-powered smart agriculture decision-support platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. The project aims to help farmers adapt to changing climate conditions by using NASA Earth observation data and agricultural information to support informed crop-selection and crop-rotation
decisions.

The platform brings together environmental factors such as temperature, rainfall and water availability with local soil conditions, crop characteristics and farming priorities. It aims to help users explore suitable crop options and compare potential crop-rotation strategies based on their region and agricultural requirements.

By transforming Earth observation data into understandable agricultural insights, SQUADX aims to make climate-related farming decisions easier and more accessible. The project is important because changing weather patterns, water scarcity and declining soil health create major challenges for agriculture. Our goal is to encourage more sustainable, resource-efficient and climate-resilient farming practices through data-driven decision support.
details:
Project Details – AgriSmart (SQUADX)

1. What does your project do or how does it work?

AgriSmart is a smart agriculture platform that combines NASA satellite data, weather information, soil analysis, and machine learning to help farmers make informed farming decisions. Farmers can locate their fields using GPS, monitor vegetation health through Landsat imagery and NDVI, analyse soil conditions, assess climate risks, and explore suitable crop recommendations. It also provides AI-based crop disease detection, 3D field visualization, and multilingual voice assistance.

2. What benefits does your project have?

AgriSmart makes satellite-based agricultural information accessible through a single platform. It helps farmers monitor field conditions, plan crop rotations, identify potential climate risks, and make better use of available soil and water resources.

3. What is the intended impact of your project?

Our goal is to promote sustainable and climate-resilient agriculture by connecting NASA Earth-observation technology with practical farming needs. We aim to help farmers reduce climate-related risks and make data-driven agricultural decisions.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

We used the following technologies:

  • Frontend: React 19, JavaScript, Vite, and Tailwind CSS for building the responsive web dashboard.
  • Backend & Machine Learning: Python 3.11, FastAPI, Uvicorn, and Scikit-learn for data processing, APIs, and ML-based features.
  • NASA & Agricultural Data: NASA POWER API, Landsat 8/9 through Microsoft Planetary Computer STAC, ISRIC SoilGrids, and Open-Meteo.
  • Mapping & 3D Visualization: Leaflet, Leaflet-Geoman, Esri Satellite Imagery, and Three.js for interactive farm mapping and 3D field visualization.
  • Blockchain & Security: Solidity 0.8.20, Web3, SHA-256, and Merkle Trees for smart contracts and tamper-evident agricultural records.
  • Mobile Development: Capacitor, Android Studio, Gradle, and Java for the Android application, with smartphone GPS support.
  • Authentication & Deployment: Firebase Authentication, GitHub, Vercel, and Railway.

No separate external hardware or sensors were required; the mobile application uses the smartphone's built-in GPS.

5. How is your project creative or innovative?

AgriSmart combines NASA satellite monitoring, machine learning, soil analysis, 3D field visualization, and blockchain technology in one agriculture platform. It also provides multilingual support and a dedicated Android application, making advanced agricultural insights easier to access.

6. What factors did your team consider?

We considered temperature, rainfall, soil properties, water availability, vegetation health, crop suitability, climate risks, farmer accessibility, and local-language support while designing the platform.
